intro.label: Pocket
intro.body: Kit and bass are barely in — the first downbeat is almost empty air before the groove clicks.

intro.label: Figure
intro.body: Treat bar 0 as a count-off: leave the low E unspoken, then land the E–B–E–Bb pickup into Groove A.

intro.label: Harmony
intro.body: Em center (i). Nothing to outline yet — the ear waits for the tonic pedal.

intro.label: Missable
intro.body: Don’t fill the open. The gambling swagger starts when the chromatic Bb answers the E, not before.

a1.label: Pocket
a1.body: ~123 BPM 4/4. Kit is four-on-floor (kick every quarter) with snare accents on 2+4; hats pulse on the beat — not LAP-style 8th hats. Bass speaks on the beat with little push.

a1.label: Figure
a1.body: Core figure: E on beats 1 & 3, B (or Bb neighbor) answering. Hear E–B–E–Bb as tonic with a chromatic upper-neighbor tease.

a1.label: Harmony
a1.body: Em / Em7 home. Occasional A7 or Am color when the bass hangs on A/Bb — keep chord quality (7 vs triad) when you hear the flat-7.

a1.label: Missable
a1.body: The Bb is a chromatic neighbor, not a key change. Don’t re-root the bar on Bb; it ornaments E.

verse.label: Pocket
verse.body: Back to medium drum weight — same four-on-floor kick + snare 2+4. Bass leans harder on Bb hangs before resolving to E.

verse.label: Figure
verse.body: Bb–Bb–Bb–A into A–E–B–E. Chromatic hang, then a clean Em outline.

verse.label: Harmony
verse.body: Em answered by Am (iv) and A7 colors. Keep Am vs Am7 / A7 quality from the template when the 7th is clear.

verse.label: Missable
verse.body: The long Bb is a delay of tonic, not a new tonal center — resolve it to E on purpose.

a2.label: Pocket
a2.body: Same pocket as A — four-on-floor kick with snare on 2+4; hats sit on the quarters, not a wall of 8ths. Bass stays on the grid.

a2.label: Figure
a2.body: E pedal with Bb–A walkbacks. Lock the octave: low E, then the neighbor cluster above.

a2.label: Harmony
a2.body: Still Em-centric. When chroma leans Am/A7, it’s iv / V-of-iv flavor over the same bass story.

a2.label: Missable
a2.body: Mute the bass (S/M) and check: the ‘C7’ mirage is often just Bb in the bass against Em.

b1.label: Pocket
b1.body: Drum energy lifts (~bars 17–25) but stays four-on-floor + snare 2+4 — denser ornaments, same pulse. Ride it without rushing the E pedal.

b1.label: Figure
b1.body: More E repeats per bar (E–E–E–x) — a lift pedal — then Gb/F chromatic crumbs as tension.

b1.label: Harmony
b1.body: Em / Em7 with brief E major color flashes. Preserve Em7 when the flat-7 is audible.

b1.label: Missable
b1.body: The lift is density, not a new key. Keep E as gravity; Gb is passing, not a modulation.

chorus.label: Pocket
chorus.body: Build densifies again on the same four-on-floor grid; stay behind the beat slightly so the walk doesn’t get stiff against the kit.

chorus.label: Figure
chorus.body: Walk fragments (G–Gb–F, F–E…) into E pedals — approach notes into tonic.

chorus.label: Harmony
chorus.body: Em with B7 (V) approaches. Prefer B7 over vague diminished labels when the leading tone resolves to E.

chorus.label: Missable
chorus.body: Walk tones are approach notes — name the target chord (Em), not every passing PC.

br.label: Pocket
br.body: Bar 26 drums duck — a one-bar breath — then the kit returns. Feel the drop as intentional air.

br.label: Figure
br.body: E figures continue through the drop; don’t stop the bass just because the kit thins.

br.label: Harmony
br.body: Em pedal through the drop. Use the thin bar to hear bass alone against residual harmony.

br.label: Missable
br.body: Phone tip: loop the drop bar and toggle D&B vs full — the pocket hole is the lesson.

a3.body: Back to medium drum weight — same four-on-floor kick + snare 2+4. Bass leans harder on Bb hangs before resolving to E.

a3.label: Figure

a3.label: Harmony

a3.label: Missable

b2.body: Build densifies again on the same four-on-floor grid; stay behind the beat slightly so the walk doesn’t get stiff against the kit.

b2.label: Figure

b2.label: Harmony

out.label: Pocket
out.body: Energy fades; drums and bass thin toward silence. Let notes get shorter as the kit disappears.

out.label: Figure
out.body: Return of E/Bb neighbor language, then sparse E–B–E into air.

out.label: Harmony
out.body: Em to the end. No late modulations — chromatic bass over i.

out.label: Missable
out.body: Last bars are vocabulary of leaving: play less, not a final fill. Empty kit is the cadence.
